transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

I came in because I’ve been having these really unwanted thoughts while working on a memorial piece for my aunt. I keep worrying that if I choose the wrong photo or color or arrange something badly, it means I’m dishonoring her or that I didn’t love her enough. It feels more intense than normal creative doubt, and I can’t really just brush it off.
Do these anxious thoughts and worries only happen when you're working on the memorial piece, or do you also find yourself feeling this way in other parts of your life?

It’s mostly been with the memorial piece. That’s where it really hit me—the thoughts about getting a photo placement or color wrong and then feeling like that would somehow mean I was dishonoring my aunt or didn’t love her enough. I haven’t been able to just treat it like normal creative doubt.
Have you noticed any similar worries or anxiety in other parts of your life, such as work, relationships, or other decisions, or does it seem limited to working on the memorial piece?

It seems pretty limited to the memorial piece. That’s where I keep getting stuck with these unwanted thoughts—like if I choose the wrong photo or color, or place something the wrong way, it somehow means I’m dishonoring my aunt or didn’t love her enough. I know it sounds extreme, but I haven’t been able to just shrug it off like normal creative second-guessing.

When you have these worries about the memorial piece, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking, redoing parts, or trying to mentally ‘fix’ things—to try to feel better or prevent something bad from happening?

Yes. I’ll reread the label text again and again, and I keep nudging the same objects on the table like they’re not quite right. I also check the layout photos over and over until it finally feels “settled.” Part of me knows it’s probably already fine, but I still do it, and then I end up losing a lot of studio time.
Outside of working on the memorial piece, do these worries or rituals interfere with your daily life, like your work, relationships, or other activities?

Mostly it’s tied to the memorial piece, not everything else. I’m still getting most of my work done, but the time I keep losing in the studio has started to matter. I missed a grant deadline because of it, and I backed out of a gallery talk I actually wanted to do. So it’s not taking over my whole life, but it is interfering.

When you check the layout photos or nudge the objects on the table, is it because you feel anxious and need to reduce that anxiety, or because you think something bad might happen if you don’t do it just right?

It’s mostly that anxious, unsettled feeling. I reread the label, nudge the objects, and check the photos because it feels like I can’t leave it alone until it feels “right” or settled. I don’t fully believe anything bad will happen, and part of me knows it’s probably already fine, but I still keep doing it and lose studio time.
Would you say the main reason you keep checking and adjusting things is to relieve the anxious feeling, even if you know it might not make sense?

Yes, that’s basically it. I keep rereading the label, adjusting the same objects, and looking at the layout photos because I’m trying to get rid of that unsettled feeling. I know, logically, it’s probably already fine, but I still can’t quite leave it alone until it feels settled, and then I’ve lost a bunch of studio time.
Do these thoughts about the memorial piece feel intrusive or unwanted, like they’re not really who you are, even though you still feel compelled to act on them?

Yes. They feel really unwanted. It’s not how I want to think about my aunt or the piece. I’ll suddenly get this thought that if I place a photo wrong, or choose the wrong color, it means I’m dishonoring her or that I didn’t love her enough. And I know that sounds extreme, because normally I can handle creative uncertainty, but with this I can’t just brush it off. It feels intrusive, like it doesn’t fit with who I am, but I still feel pushed to fix it.

Outside of the memorial piece, do you find yourself worrying excessively about other events or activities, such as work, health, or other responsibilities, even when there isn’t a clear reason to be concerned?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I have normal worries about work or deadlines sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed the same kind of excessive worrying across everything. The main thing I’ve been stuck on is the memorial piece.
Have you noticed any impact on your mood, focus, or ability to function in daily life outside of working on the memorial piece, such as trouble sleeping, irritability, or difficulty concentrating?

I’m still functioning for the most part. I’m getting most of my work done. But the time I lose in the studio has started to matter — I missed a grant deadline because of it, and I also backed out of a gallery talk I’d actually wanted to do. So it’s not stopping everything, but it is affecting things.
